- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop too sharply, missing sustained upward trends.
- Model underestimates prices during sharp downward moves (e.g., 70s to 68s), often failing to recognize volatility spikes.
- Mean reversion is overemphasized — model assumes prices will return to historical averages too quickly.
- Overshoots after spikes are common — model reacts too aggressively to short-term volatility, leading to inflated forecasts.
- Forecast horizon 30d is overly sensitive to recent volatility; model reacts to noise rather than structural trends.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of price increases during periods of high demand or policy tightening.
- Model fails to capture lagged effects — e.g., policy changes or supply shocks that take 2–3 days to fully materialize.
- Forecasts are too optimistic in the final 5–10 days, often missing the “tail” of a trend or sudden correction.
